segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good morning, and welcome to Oniton Hall, one of the largest estates in the area.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My name's Nick, and I’m one of the guides.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’ll give you a brief introduction to the estate while you’re sitting down, and then we'll walk round.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The estate consists of the house, gardens, parkland and farm, and it dates back to the fourteenth century.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The original house was replaced in the late seventeenth century, and of course it has had a large number of owners.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Almost all of them have left their mark, generally by adding new rooms, like the ballroom and conservatory, or by demolishing others.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The farm looks much as it’s always done, although the current owner has done a great deal of work to the flower beds.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the seventeenth century, the estate was owned by a very wealthy man called Sir Edward Downes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: His intention was to escape from the world of politics, after years as an active politician, and to build a new house worthy of his big collection of books, paintings and sculptures.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: He broke off contact with his former political allies, and hosted meetings of creative and literary people, like painters and poets.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Unusually for his time, he didn’t care whether his guests were rich or poor, as long as they had talent.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Big houses like Oniton had dozens of servants until the 1920s or 30s, and we’ve tried to show what their working lives were like.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Photographs of course don't give much of an idea, so instead, as you go round the house, you’ll see volunteers dressed up as nineteenth-century servants, going about their work.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They’ll explain what they're doing, and tell you their recipes, or what tools they’re using.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve just introduced this feature to replace the audio guide we used to have available.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I see there are a number of children here with you today.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, we have several activities specially for children, like dressing up in the sorts of clothes that children wore in the past, and as it's a fine day, some of you will probably want to play in the adventure playground.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Our latest addition is child-sized tractors, that you can drive around the grounds.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ll also be going into the farm that’s part of the estate, where there’s plenty to do.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most of the buildings date from the eighteenth century, so you can really step back into an agricultural past.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Until recently, the dairy was where milk from the cows was turned into cheese.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s now the place to go for lunch, or afternoon tea, or just a cup of coffee and a slice of homemade cake.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The big stone building that dominates the farm is the large barn, and in here is our collection of agricultural tools.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These were used in the past to plough the earth, sow seeds, make gates, and much more.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There's a small barn, also made of stone, where you can groom the donkeys and horses, to keep their coats clean.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They really seem to enjoy having it done, and children love grooming them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The horses no longer live in the stables, which instead is the place to go to buy gifts, books. our own jams and pickles, and clothes and blankets made of wool from our sheep.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Outside the shed, which is the only brick building, you can climb into a horse-drawn carriage for a lovely, relaxing tour of the park and farm.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The carriages are well over a hundred years old.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And finally, the parkland, which was laid out in the eighteenth century, with a lake and trees that are now well established.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You’ll see types of cattle and sheep that are hardly ever found on farms these days.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We're helping to preserve them, to stop their numbers falling further.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK, well if you'd like to come with me ...
